one_liner: Research rank/select bit vector with worst-case constant-time select at about 0.8 percent space overhead, far below SDSL, sux and pasta.
what_it_does: Adds rank and select support to a plain uncompressed bit vector while keeping the extra index tiny (0.82 percent of the input in the checked-in runs). The structure is the class m3 (m3.hpp plus the sample tree in Tree3.hpp) behind an abstract Bitvector interface with rank_1, rank_0, select_1, select_0, access and space_in_bits; only rank_0, rank_1 and select_1 are implemented. It is not a drop-in library: m3 has no constructor taking data and reads the input from global vectors (bits, N_bits, N_words) declared in bv.hpp and filled by the bv.cpp benchmark driver, and its tuning is chosen with compile-time CMake macros.
how_it_is_fast: It pairs a summary tree (per-superblock counters: 64 Ki-bit superblocks of 32 L0 blocks of 2048 bits, with 12-bit relative L0 counts unpacked with SSE/AVX2 shuffles and compared in SIMD) with a compressed three-level sample tree that stores positions of some 1-bits, which bounds select to a constant number of steps in the worst case. Blocks whose minority bits are rare are stored sparsely as 11-bit position lists and dense blocks verbatim, and the final in-word step uses PDEP/TZCNT. Prefetch hints and 2 MiB transparent huge pages (madvise) cut cache and TLB misses.
when_to_use: Very large static bit vectors (around 1e9 bits and up) where the rank/select index must stay under 1 percent of the bits, e.g. succinct trees, FM-index or wavelet-tree building blocks under tight memory.
Workloads that need worst-case constant select time, including adversarial or very uneven densities where sampling-based select (sux simple_select, SDSL mcl) can degrade.
x86-64 machines with AVX2 and BMI2 (Haswell or Zen 2 and later) built with -march=native.
As a reference design for engineering your own low-overhead select: the code exposes many compile-time variants (L0 size 512/1024/2048, tree strategies, prefetch and huge-page switches).
when_not_to_use: When select latency matters more than space: in the repo's own runs at 0.82 percent overhead select_1 took about 95-100 ns; at density 0.5 that is level with sux rank9sel (88 ns) and simple_select s1 (91 ns) and slower than SDSL mcl (about 81-85 ns) and simple_select s3 (about 49 ns at 7 percent overhead). It only pulls ahead at density 0.02, where pasta flat (144 ns) and SDSL mcl (185 ns) slow down.
If you need select_0 or access: m3::select_0 and m3::access are stubs that return 0.
Non-x86 targets (ARM, RISC-V) or x86 without AVX2/BMI2: the code includes x86intrin.h and uses _mm256_*, _pdep_u64 and _lzcnt_u64 unconditionally.
Dynamic bit vectors: the index is built once (build_auxiliaries) over a static input.
If you want a packaged dependency: there is no install target, no tests beyond the driver's validate mode, 15 commits, 5 stars.

integration.dependencies: none for m3 itself beyond the repo's bv.hpp, alignedallocator.hpp, constants.hpp and Tree3.hpp; the benchmark driver also pulls vendored pasta and tlx and clones sdsl-lite, sux, rankselect and rankselect2 at HEAD
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (std::popcount, constexpr std::string), CMake 3.28; logs show Clang 18.1.3
integration.platforms: x86-64 only, AVX2 + BMI2 + LZCNT required (built with -march=native); Linux (madvise MADV_HUGEPAGE via sys/mman.h)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; queries are const member functions but the class reads process-wide globals, so one structure per process in practice
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same rank_1/select_1 semantics as SDSL or sux, but different interface, input taken from global vectors, and no select_0/access

gotchas: m3::access(i) and m3::select_0(k) are unimplemented and silently return 0; calling them gives wrong answers rather than an error.

Input is not passed in: m3 builds from the globals bits / N_bits / N_words (declared extern in bv.hpp, defined in bv.cpp), so extracting it into another project means rewiring those globals or editing the class.

Macro typo in m3::rank_1: '#if REVERSE==2 && POP==2 && CUSTOM_LO != 512' tests CUSTOM_LO (letter O), which is undefined and evaluates to 0, so the intended exclusion for 512-bit L0 blocks never applies; it affects rank_1 only with CUSTOM_L0=512 (the 3.2 percent configuration) and was not exercised by the select-only checked-in runs. Run the driver's 'valid' job (compares every query against a naive structure) before trusting a non-default configuration.

Benchmark caveats: single instance, single iteration per point, random uniform densities only (indep generator), FORCE_CRIT_PATH makes queries dependent (latency, not throughput), and competitors are cloned at their current heads, so reruns may not match the logs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over SPIDER (about 3.8 percent overhead), orzo and pasta flat when the index size must be under 1 percent and you only need rank_1/select_1; pick SPIDER, QuadRank/BiRank or splatlab's PTSelect when query speed or throughput is the priority, and LA-vector or h0_bv when the bit vector itself should be compressed.
verified_claims_summary: Checked-in multibench_out logs (1e9 random bits at densities 0.5, 0.2 and 0.02, 2e7 dependent random select_1 queries, one run each, Clang 18.1.3 -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG, Intel Core i9-13900H) show m3 at 0.82 percent overhead and 95-96 ns per select, against pasta flat 3.58 percent, sux simple_select s1 2.34 percent, SDSL mcl about 23 percent and rank9sel about 50-56 percent, at 76-185 ns for those competitors; the space win (about 2.9x to 95x less overhead, derived from page data) is the result, not speed. The paper's 0.78 percent and 4.5x to 64.1x figures come from a search snippet of arXiv 2509.17819 (blocked here).
status_note: Active (README edited 2026-09-15, code last changed 2025-09-21), MPL-2.0 so files can be vendored with file-level copyleft; research code from the KIT group (Kurpicz, Rigi-Luperti, Sanders) that needs extraction work before use outside its benchmark driver.
